citation: Resendez, M., Azin, M., & Strobel, A. (2009). A study on the effects of Pearson's 2009 enVisionMATH program: Final summative report. Jackson, WY: PRES Associates, Inc. (Two-year cumulative findings of the enVisionMATH efficacy RCT; the Year-1 source is Resendez, M., & Azin, M. (2008). A study on the effects of Pearson's 2009 enVisionMATH program. 2007-2008: First year report. Jackson, WY: PRES Associates, Inc.)
report_number: PRES Associates enVisionMATH efficacy study (Pearson Education curriculum efficacy RCT); reviewed in WWC Elementary School Mathematics Intervention Report: enVisionMATH (Jan 2013), ERIC ED538671.
design: Cluster (teacher/class-level) randomized controlled trial. Teachers in grades 2-5 were randomly assigned WITHIN each participating school to teach the 2009 Pearson enVisionMATH core elementary math curriculum (treatment) or to continue with the school's existing/business-as-usual math curriculum (control). The TPD-for-curricula component: enVisionMATH treatment teachers received ~5-6 hours of training from a Pearson professional trainer before implementation, a 3-hour follow-up within 2-3 weeks, and at several sites 1-2 additional 3-4 hour follow-up sessions, plus embedded implementation guidelines/monitoring; control teachers received no such PD. The RCT commenced Fall 2007 in grades 2 & 4 (2007-08, Year 1 = First Year Report, Resendez & Azin 2008) and followed the SAME students into grades 3 & 5 (2008-09, Year 2 = Final Summative Report, Resendez, Azin & Strobel 2009). Setting: originally 8 geographically dispersed elementary schools in 8 states (CO, KY, MA, MT, NH, NC, OH, TN); Year 1 analytic sample = 1,156 students / 54 teachers (29 treatment, 30 control). For Year 2, two schools adopted new math curricula school-wide and dropped out, leaving 6 schools; Year 2 analytic sample = 708 students retained across both years (330 treatment, 378 control); the WWC-validated Year 2 outcome (MAT8 Concepts & Problem-Solving) had n=681 in 6 schools. Outcome subject = mathematics (-> STEM); grades 2-5 (mixed). Analyses via multilevel/HLM modeling with students nested in teachers/classrooms (unit of analysis matches unit of random assignment), adjusting for pretest and covariates -> clustering accounted for.
problems: OPEN-FULL-TEXT LIMITATION: The actual Resendez, Azin & Strobel (2009) Final Summative Report PDF is NOT openly available. The original was hosted on Pearson's site (pearsoned.com/wp-content/uploads/) but only the Year-1 First Year Report (Sept 2008) and a separate ELL/minorities QED special report are preserved on the Wayback Machine; the Year-2/summative PDF is not archived anywhere I could find (checked eric.ed.gov, Google Scholar, presassociates.com, and ~15 Wayback filename variants). The PDF saved to disk (data/fulltext/resendez_azin_2009.pdf) is therefore the WWC Elementary School Mathematics Intervention Report: enVisionMATH (Jan 2013, ERIC ED538671), which is the authoritative OPEN document that independently re-reviewed BOTH waves of this exact study and reports WWC-recalculated effect sizes, posttest means/SDs, and sample sizes. I also retrieved and read the full Year-1 First Year Report from the Wayback Machine (Sept 2008) to confirm the design, randomization level, TPD/training structure, measures, and the authors' own Year-1 between-group HLM effect sizes (d=0.21 MAT8 Computation, 0.24 GMADE, 0.20 BAM, p.41) -- these corroborate the WWC's recalculated Year-1 ESs. STUDY-IDENTITY / 2008-vs-2009 NUANCE: The WWC treats 'Resendez & Azin 2008' (First Year Report, Year 1, grades 2&4) and 'Resendez, Azin & Strobel 2009' (Final Summative Report, Year 2, grades 3&5) as a SINGLE 2-year study with two waves; the 2009 report is the END-OF-STUDY document presenting the cumulative two-year findings. This is distinct from a separate later 2012 Resendez & Azin study. Per the spec's timepoint rule ('if the study spans multiple years, take the end-of-treatment wave'), the HEADLINE/primary effect size is the Year-2 (2008-09) contrast (g #1 below, MAT8 Concepts & Problem-Solving, the ONLY Year-2 measure the WWC validated without reservations). The four Year-1 (2007-08) contrasts are also recorded (g #2-#5) as earlier-wave secondary contrasts from the same study for traceability/robustness, clearly labeled timepoint='post Y1'. ATTRITION/Y2 MEASURES: The 2009 Year-2 analysis reported four math measures, but three failed WWC standards due to high attrition and baseline non-equivalence; only MAT8 Concepts & Problem-Solving meets standards, and only its numbers are published in the open WWC report (Appendix D), so I extract only that one Year-2 g. CLUSTER/ICC: The authors' HLM accounts for student-within-teacher clustering (cluster_adjusted=true), but no design-effect ICC is reported in any open source -> icc=null (not guessed). Year-2 exact treatment/control split per measure and exact teacher (cluster) count are not given in the open WWC report; n_clusters is left null for Year-2 (6 schools noted) and set to 54 for Year-1. VARIANCE: The WWC reports effect sizes and p-values but no SE on the ES metric; g_var/g_se below are computed from the posttest means/SDs/Ns (Var(d)=(nt+nc)/(nt*nc)+d^2/(2(nt+nc)), Var(g)=J^2*Var(d)) -- these are NOT cluster-corrected variances, so central re-analysis may need to inflate them by a design effect (no ICC available). TEST-TYPE: outcomes are norm-referenced commercial/standardized instruments (MAT8 by Harcourt, GMADE by Pearson Assessment, BAM by CTB), labeled standardized_independent, EXCEPT the 2nd-grade BAM and the open-ended composite which were partly researcher-adapted (labeled unclear).

effect_sizes.arm_label: enVisionMATH curriculum + Pearson teacher PD vs business-as-usual existing math curriculum (Year 2 / end of 2-year exposure, 2008-09)
effect_sizes.test_name: Metropolitan Achievement Test 8 (MAT8), Form V, Math Concepts and Problem-Solving subtest (Harcourt Assessment; norm-referenced)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post Y2 (spring 2009, end of two-year cumulative exposure; immediate post-intervention end-of-treatment wave)
effect_sizes.g_method: d = (Mt - Mc)/s_pooled with WWC-reported Year-2 posttest means/SDs (Mt=684.57, SDt=60.34; Mc=673.14, SDc=50.51; WWC Appendix D, p.10): s_pooled = sqrt(((330-1)*60.34^2+(378-1)*50.51^2)/(330+378-2)) = 55.31, d = 11.43/55.31 = 0.2067; Hedges g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*706-1) = 0.99894, g = 0.2064 ~ 0.207, matching the WWC-reported ES of 0.21 (the WWC value derives from the study's HLM impact, which accounts for student-within-teacher clustering). g_var/g_se from Var(d)=(nt+nc)/(nt*nc)+d^2/(2(nt+nc)), Var(g)=J^2*Var(d) using the n=708 retained-sample split (330/378); NOTE this analytic variance is NOT cluster-corrected (no ICC available). Exact per-measure split is approximate (WWC lists n=681 for this measure; final retained sample 708 = 330 T / 378 C).
effect_sizes.page_ref: WWC report (ED538671) Appendix D, p.10 (Year-2 supplemental finding, Resendez & Azin 2009): MAT8 Concepts & Problem-Solving, grades 3&5, 6 schools/681 students, int M=684.57(60.34), comp M=673.14(50.51), mean diff 11.43, ES 0.21, improvement index +8, p=0.00.
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY end-of-treatment (Year-2, 2008-09) TPD-vs-control student math achievement contrast = the headline finding of the 2009 Final Summative Report. enVisionMATH students outscored control by ES=0.21 (improvement index +8, p<.001) on the MAT8 Concepts & Problem-Solving subtest after two cumulative years. This is the ONLY Year-2 measure the WWC validated without reservations (no clustering or multiple-comparison correction was needed per WWC's Y2 review); the study's other three Year-2 math measures failed WWC standards due to high attrition and baseline non-equivalence and are not reported with usable numbers in the open WWC document. WWC rated the overall program 'potentially positive effects, small extent of evidence' for math achievement based primarily on the Year-1 wave.

effect_sizes.g_method: d = (99.55-97.21)/s_pooled; s_pooled = sqrt(((559-1)*10.25^2+(559-1)*10.59^2)/(1118-2)) = 10.42, d = 2.34/10.42 = 0.2245; Hedges g = J*d, J=0.99933 (df=1116), g=0.2244 ~ matches WWC-reported ES 0.22 (Appendix C, p.9) and the authors' own HLM d=0.24 (First Year Report p.41). g_var/g_se from analytic-variance formula (NOT cluster-corrected). Treatment/control split ~50/50 approximated (WWC n=1118 for this measure; 29 treatment vs 30 control teachers).
effect_sizes.page_ref: WWC report (ED538671) Appendix C, p.9 (Resendez & Azin 2008): GMADE Concepts & Communication, grades 2&4, 8 schools/1118 students, int M=99.55(10.25), comp M=97.21(10.59), mean diff 2.34, ES 0.22, improvement index +9, p=0.01. effect_sizes.notes: Earlier-wave (Year 1) TPD-vs-control contrast from the same 2-year study, on math vocabulary/language. Statistically significant positive effect. Recorded for traceability; the Year-2 MAT8 C&PS contrast (g #1) is the end-of-treatment primary per spec.
